summary.text: A 62-year-old man, an active smoker with no other significant past medical history, presented with a one-week history of recurrent palpitations and intermittent non-exertional chest discomfort. He was hemodynamically stable on arrival; the admission ECG showed sinus rhythm with frequent PVCs, and monitoring recorded a brief self-terminating wide-complex tachycardia consistent with NSVT.

Coronary angiography showed no obstructive coronary artery disease. Laboratory testing before CMR found normal electrolytes, renal function, thyroid profile and cardiac biomarkers, and an invasive electrophysiology study was not pursued at this stage. Ambulatory rhythm monitoring later showed additional PVCs and short NSVT runs.

CMR showed preserved biventricular size and systolic function with an LVEF of 65%, bi-leaflet mitral valve prolapse with moderate eccentric regurgitation, and a 6 mm systolic separation confirming mitral annular disjunction. Native T1 was elevated, T2 mapping and STIR showed no edema, and LGE showed focal fibrosis of the anterolateral papillary muscle with an inferolateral mid-myocardial stripe.

The findings supported a diagnosis of arrhythmic mitral valve prolapse syndrome. He was started on beta-blocker therapy and referred urgently to cardiac electrophysiology for sudden cardiac death risk stratification. A close follow-up plan with ambulatory rhythm monitoring was established, and the primary-prevention ICD indication will be re-evaluated.
